rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: The law against a dangerously out-of-control dog applies in public places, private places and the owner's home.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: A dog may be dangerously out of control if it injures someone or makes someone reasonably fear injury.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: Pit Bull Terrier, Japanese Tosa, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro and XL Bully are banned types.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: It is illegal to possess an XL Bully in England and Wales without a valid Certificate of Exemption.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: Exempt banned dogs must be microchipped and neutered.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: An exempt banned dog must be kept on a lead and muzzled in public.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: The lead for an XL Bully in public must be securely held by a person aged at least 16.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: Exempt dogs must be kept securely so they cannot escape.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: Owners must provide access to read the dog's microchip when required by an authorised officer.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: Owners must provide the Certificate of Exemption when requested, either immediately or within five days.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: Owners must notify Defra of permanent address changes.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: Owners must notify Defra if the dog dies or is exported.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: An XL Bully may be kept at a different address for no more than 30 days in a 12-month period under the published rules.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: It is illegal to sell, give away, abandon, allow to stray or breed from an XL Bully.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: Applications for ordinary XL Bully Certificates of Exemption have closed; new exemptions require a court order.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: Third-party public-liability insurance is no longer required for banned breed dogs from 1 July 2026.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: Police and local authorities can use criminal and civil powers to address dangerous dogs and nuisance behaviour.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: Whether a dog is a banned type depends on physical characteristics and formal enforcement assessment, not only its stated breed.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: The child-supervision condition for banned dogs in private places starts on 1 November 2026 and is not yet in force on 26 July 2026.

rows.source: Defra dangerous-dog and XL Bully guidance
rows.verified: Dangerous-dog law is person-, animal- and incident-specific and is not converted into parcel-level probability.
